title: Trump's new tariffs would put rates right back where they were before the Supreme Court stepped in
summary:
A new wave of tariffs from the White House would move overall rates almost exactly back to where they stood in early 2026, according to one initial analysis of the new duties.
The Yale Budget Lab says the newly unveiled plans, if enacted, would return the US to rates seen just before the Supreme Court struck down President Trump's blanket tariffs in February.
The rate in February, just before the high court struck down Trump's tariffs enacted under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act of 1977 (IEEPA), was 13.8%.
That remains well below the overall rates seen in 2025.
The group estimates that 2025 rates exceeded 15%, peaking at nearly 23% in the weeks after "Liberation Day" in April 2025.

title: US announces new tariffs of up to 20% on China, the EU, and 12 other nations
summary:
The Trump administration on Wednesday proposed new tariffs of up to 20% on China, the European Union, and 12 other major US trading partners to take effect next year, following an eight-month investigation into excess manufacturing capacity.
The proposed 20% tariff on many Chinese goods was described by the Trump administration as a "deal rate" that could go higher depending on how ongoing talks progress.

title: What Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia teaches China's Xi about Trump
summary:
Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO has riveted the world - including China, where it has become the top trending post on Weibo, the country's biggest social media platform.
But to many, Huang's return, which is being dubbed one of the greatest U-turns of all time, seems like a vindication for China.
Beijing has dismissed claims that one of the women who had an affair with Jensen Huang had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, its version of the CIA, as a spy.
Chinese state media has also framed the spy saga as a smear campaign orchestrated by China hawks in Washington.
Now the White House, and President Donald Trump himself, have said Huang poses no national security threat, although investigations into the spy allegations are still ongoing.

title: Five Russian military jets hit in airfield strike, says Ukraine
summary:
Ukraine has said it damaged five Russian military aircraft in an attack on Russia's Savasleyka airfield, 300km (185 miles) east of Moscow.
It did not elaborate on what weapons it had used to hit the airfield.
The airfield at Savasleyka, in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region, has been a target for Ukraine for several years.
"Without fuel, military vehicles cannot move; without ammunition, artillery falls silent," the defence ministry said, adding that every successful hit meant Moscow could carry out fewer strikes.
Ten people were killed across several regions between 24 and 25 November, while thousands are without power after Russian strikes on energy infrastructure.

title: Oil prices rise after Houthis claim attack on Saudi refinery
summary:
By Nicole Jao and Anna HirtensteinNEW YORK, Nov 25 (Reuters) - Crude oil prices rallied on Wednesday after Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery, raising concerns about unexpected Middle ‌East supply disruptions that could cut against expectations for a coming global surplus.
Brent crude futures settled $3.21, or 3.5%, ‌higher at $94.61 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures climbed $1.63, or 2%, to $83.68.
Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis ​said on Wednesday that they had attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery and Riyadh's financial district.
The refinery, Saudi Arabia's largest, is part of a complex that also serves as a major export terminal for Saudi crude.
The Houthi statement triggered Wednesday's price rally, said PVM oil analyst Tamas Varga, citing a rising geopolitical risk premium.

title: Russia's own figures show it has lost nearly 500,000 people in Ukraine war
summary:
At least 490,334 Russian soldiers have died since the start of the war in Ukraine in 2022, according to Russian government statistics analysed by the BBC.
The leaked Rosstat data reveal how the full-scale invasion of Ukraine has fundamentally changed mortality patterns in Russia, and show the high cost paid in human life in a war that Vladimir Putin had assumed would last only days but is now almost five years old.
Russia's statistics agency admitted to a cyber-attack, but denied any protected information had been leaked.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Wednesday that only Russia's defence ministry could officially report data on losses: "I suggest no other data be taken into account."
The defence ministry has not released any official casualty figures for several years.

title: Clashing political visions reflect a divided Spain ahead of election
summary:
Speaking in a wrestling ring on the island of Tenerife as he campaigned ahead of Sunday's general election, Spain's Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez cautioned those listening about the spread of right-wing governments.
"What good has President [Donald] Trump done the United States and, by extension, the world - was he a change or a step backwards?"
he asked supporters, before invoking the administrations of Brazil's former leader, Jair Bolsonaro, and Argentinian President Javier Milei.
The election comes amid a deeply polarised political atmosphere in which both left and right have warned about their opponents' ability to undermine democracy.
In a Europe dominated by right-leaning governments, Sánchez has gained a reputation as the continent's most outspoken and uncompromising left-wing prime minister.

title: Pakistani astronaut to become first foreign visitor to China’s space station
summary:

title: North Korea expels Swiss diplomat in sanctions row
summary:
North Korea has ordered Switzerland's diplomatic representative to leave the country within 48 hours and called for the office to close, in a row over sanctions.
Confirming the expulsion, KCNA said: "The Foreign Ministry of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea) declared the head of the Swiss Diplomatic Office in the DPRK persona non grata and urged him to leave the country within 48 hours."
The diplomatic rebuke comes weeks after Swiss foreign minister Ignazio Cassis made a rare visit to North Korea, where he officially reopened the office and discussed normalising relations.
Swiss authorities said relations between the two countries would be maintained through the North Korean embassy in Bern, and the Swiss embassy in Beijing.
Diplomatic links with North Korea were first established in 1974 and Switzerland opened a co-operation office in Pyongyang in 1997.
